name: ProtocolQA
intro: ProtocolQA是LAB-Bench中的135题无工具多项选择子任务。第一轮生物学专家从protocols.io与STAR Protocols提取方案，注入一个或多个会明确改变或破坏结果的错误并解释影响；另一批专家检查错误与解释是否对齐、是否会产生负面结果，再撰写包含假想实验结果与修复措施的选择题。写作者最初5–10题由作者校准，此后仍持续复核。
build_method: 两轮生物学专家依次完成方案提取与注错说明、错误对齐与负面结果核验及故障排除选择题撰写；作者校准每名写作者最初5–10题并持续复核
eval_feature: 零样本CoT、无工具、随机选项、明确拒答项和文本解析；报告Accuracy、Precision、Coverage并对完整公开与私有部分取三次运行平均，另做独立20题开放回答专家复核
scale: 135题：固定仓库划分为108题公开、27题私有；另有20题开放回答审计文件
build_method_en: Two rounds of biology experts first extract and alter protocols with an error explanation, then check error-explanation alignment and the negative outcome before drafting troubleshooting MCQs; authors calibrate each writer's first 5-10 items and continue review
eval_feature_en: Zero-shot CoT, no tools, randomized options, an explicit decline choice, and text parsing; Accuracy, Precision, and Coverage are averaged over three runs on public and private items, with a separate expert-reviewed 20-item open-answer audit
intro_en: ProtocolQA is the 135-question, tool-free multiple-choice subtask in LAB-Bench. First-round biology experts extract protocols from protocols.io and STAR Protocols, inject one or more errors that unambiguously alter or ruin the outcome, and explain the effect. Additional experts check alignment and the negative outcome before drafting a hypothetical-result troubleshooting MCQ. Authors calibrate each writer's first 5-10 questions and review items on an ongoing basis.
scale_en: 135 questions: the pinned repository split contains 108 public and 27 private IDs; a separate open-answer audit file contains 20 items

drawio_review_note: reviewed_at=2026-07-18; source_stage=paper-and-official-release alignment; scope=ProtocolQA only. The primary LAB-Bench paper is pinned to https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10362v3 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2407.10362v3. The reviewed PDF SHA256 is 7c781a703287616d6561e0ce50aed494946c7609a5a1b5985fb7849ce9e884dd. The official repository is pinned to https://github.com/Future-House/LAB-Bench/tree/998a8e0a40cf116c80e1b0e7a805ebb5fb9fa838. At that commit, README.md SHA256 is ddf807cffedfdb2dbcb5d1915367ebc77849e72dbbcdfa7dd7c7cb0779059a26, LICENSE SHA256 is 23ee78c8bae49cf08ea2f0c84945c66b987ebe4520881fb51b3dad4fb43d07c2, ProtocolQA/task.py SHA256 is 604864a1fb00734b4835c5431646ea7484f4d666ec3d214f347e63d14382bd63, protocolqa-v1-public.jsonl SHA256 is 08e85d9c0afb85a3919b78a44095eabdc031ad77652da2ccc59407a162bd63a4, protocolqa-v1-openanswer.jsonl SHA256 is 4ccc200873d4c73e07c6a0ce0b2d6010a36f47f3fbe5963b9738604116691793, and protocolqa-v1-splits.json SHA256 is 3e6774d7c05b83caa024f96a475815ca13199af0ef9f8781c639e6b5202c16f4. The construction topology follows Appendix C.5 and the shared manual-generation methods. In round one, contracted biology experts extract published protocols from protocols.io and STAR Protocols, introduce one or more errors that unambiguously alter or ruin the protocol output or an intermediate step, and provide an explanation. In round two, additional experts select an altered protocol, check that the error aligns with the explanation, check that it would produce a negative outcome, and only then draft a question built around a hypothetical experimental result and a corrective change. The shared quality process is explicit: one or more authors carefully review each new writer's first 5-10 questions, send them for rework, accept them, or remove them; questions continue to receive author review before merger into the corpus. The final ProtocolQA paper set contains 135 questions and is tool-free. It must not be confused with the 2,457-question LAB-Bench total. Evaluation uses the paper's zero-shot chain-of-thought prompt, randomly permutes answer choices, adds an explicit insufficient-information decline choice, and gives models no tools. The harness parses answer tags from text completions with a regex and uses Claude 2 as a fallback parser. Accuracy is correct answers divided by all questions, Precision is correct answers divided by attempted questions, and Coverage is attempted questions divided by all questions. Paper tables evaluate the entire dataset, including public and private splits, and average over three runs per model. Human baselining is separate and prevents experts from receiving questions they drafted. The paper's 20-item ProtocolQA open-answer audit is a separate workflow: wording is modified where needed to remove multiple-choice references, Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o completions are graded against the ideal multiple-choice answer by an expert biologist paper author, and every grade is reviewed by a second person. It reports 0.30 and 0.20 accuracy respectively. This 20-item open-answer audit is not the OpenAI ProtocolQA Open-Ended 108-item system-card evaluation. The fixed repository exposes 108 public ProtocolQA rows and lists 27 private IDs, exactly accounting for 135. The separate open-answer file has 20 rows. The graph treats these files as pinned release evidence rather than as new construction stages. The repository LICENSE is Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International, recorded as CC BY-SA 4.0 for the public package. No official leaderboard is inferred. Solid arrows encode the two expert rounds, alignment and outcome gates, MCQ drafting, calibration, ongoing review, the 135-item set, zero-shot tool-free evaluation, text parsing, three metrics, three-run report, and the paper's separate manual open-answer audit. Dashed arrows encode the fixed source card, pinned 108/27 release, license, and hashed 20-row audit file. English and Chinese specs have identical semantic IDs, types, positions, edge types, styles, waypoints, and modules; all secondary edges explicitly set dashed=true and all edges have no labels. Source-stage Mermaid fallbacks remain null or empty. Formal Draw.io, architecture JSON, SVG, PNG, catalog, manifest, and synchronization files are intentionally unchanged in this source-stage handoff.
